```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(foundryR)
```

`foundry_document_pages()` and `foundry_document_cells()` import a completed Azure AI Document Intelligence REST result. They run locally. They do not upload documents, submit analysis jobs, or replace a PDF parser. Both functions are experimental.

Use them when your existing Document Intelligence workflow produces JSON and you need text or table cells in a data frame. Keep the source document and the full result JSON. The returned rows retain source identifiers and locations, but they do not contain every field in the service response.

## Import a result

Read saved JSON without simplifying its arrays into data frames. Use an identifier from your document inventory so the result can be joined back to the source.

```{r saved-result, eval=FALSE}
result <- jsonlite::fromJSON("analysis-result.json", simplifyVector = FALSE)
pages <- foundry_document_pages(result, document_id = "report-001")
cells <- foundry_document_cells(result, document_id = "report-001")
```

The functions accept either `analyzeResult` itself or a polling response with `status = "succeeded"` and `analyzeResult`. Failed or unfinished responses raise an error.

This synthetic result shows the data shape without calling Azure:

```{r local-result}
result <- list(
  modelId = "prebuilt-layout",
  apiVersion = "2024-11-30",
  stringIndexType = "unicodeCodePoint",
  contentFormat = "text",
  content = "Hours: 12\nHours: 18",
  pages = list(
    list(pageNumber = 1L, spans = list(list(offset = 0L, length = 9L))),
    list(pageNumber = 2L, spans = list(list(offset = 10L, length = 9L)))
  ),
  tables = list(list(cells = list(list(
    rowIndex = 0L, columnIndex = 0L, content = "12",
    spans = list(list(offset = 7L, length = 2L)),
    boundingRegions = list(list(pageNumber = 1L))
  ))))
)
pages <- foundry_document_pages(result, document_id = "report-001")
pages[, c("document_id", "page_number", "text", "review_status")]

cells <- foundry_document_cells(result, document_id = "report-001")
cells[, c("document_id", "table_index", "row_index", "column_index",
          "text", "service_confidence")]
```

Table output has one row per layout cell. It keeps merged-cell spans and all bounding regions for cells that cross pages. Table indices are one-based. Row and column indices stay zero-based, matching the REST response. Custom-model fields under `documents` are not imported.

## Keep source locations through annotation

Page text is a normal character column. Pass it to `foundry_extract()` with a schema for the variables you need. The original columns, including `document_id`, `page_number`, and `spans`, stay in the output.

```{r annotate-pages, eval=FALSE}
# This step calls your configured Foundry deployment.
coded <- foundry_extract(
  pages,
  text_col = "text",
  schema = foundry_schema(
    hours = schema_number("The reported number of hours, or null if absent.")
  ),
  model = "your-deployment"
)
```

Spans always refer to the original result's top-level `content`, not to an extracted variable. Page-text slicing supports Unicode code-point, UTF-16 code-unit, and grapheme-cluster offsets. It rejects out-of-range page spans and offsets that split UTF-16 surrogate pairs. Disjoint page spans are joined without an added separator. If the service returned Markdown, the page text retains that format.

## Review before analysis

`review_status` starts as `"unreviewed"` for every row. Word confidence stays in the `words` list-column. A cell's confidence is copied to `service_confidence` when supplied, and is `NA` otherwise. The importer does not average word scores into a page confidence or interpret missing confidence as success.

A service confidence score does not validate the variables produced by a later model call. Review a sample of the source documents and annotations, record your decisions, and compare model labels with human labels using `foundry_agreement()`. See [From text to defensible estimates](annotation-workflow.html) for the annotation workflow.

The [Document Intelligence response reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/ai-services/document-intelligence/concept/analyze-document-response) describes the source objects and index conventions. Microsoft's [confidence guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/ai-services/document-intelligence/concept/accuracy-confidence) explains where service scores are available.
